definition: A model revising its own prior answer.
details: A model revising its own prior answer. Unreliable when purely intrinsic (models often keep or worsen wrong answers without new information), and effective when grounded in external feedback such as execution results, retrieved evidence, or verifier scores; reasoning RL partially trains the intrinsic version in.

explainer.lead: Self-correction is a model revising its own prior answer. It matters because revision can fix errors when grounded in new information but often fails when the model works purely from itself.

tiers.eli5: It is like checking your own homework: without the answer key you may keep the same mistake or make it worse.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers get reliable gains by grounding revision in external feedback such as execution results, retrieved evidence, or verifier scores. The pitfall is purely intrinsic self-correction, where models often keep or worsen wrong answers without new information; reasoning RL partially trains the intrinsic version in.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it is a model revising its own prior answer. Known limits: purely intrinsic self-correction is unreliable, and it is effective only when grounded in external feedback.

explainer.example: A model writes code, runs it, sees the failing test output, and revises the code based on that execution result.
